days.note_headline: Auditors will test Finance's AI agents as controls, so autonomy needs an audit trail
days.note_opening: Auditors will test AI agents as internal controls, so Treasury and Finance must evidence their autonomy. A Forbes Council article dated 16 October 2026 expects version control, segregation of duties and fallback procedur

items.headline: UOB Group sets out bounded autonomy model for agentic corporate Treasury
items.summary: UOB Group has published research on the foundations of trusted, bounded autonomy in agentic Finance, describing AI agents that run several connected tasks inside predefined mandates and policy frameworks. Treasurers get a practical template for defining what agents may do unsupervised.

items.headline: HSBC widens Treasury APIs to deliver real-time ISO 20022 account data
items.summary: HSBC has expanded its Treasury APIs, including Account Information, Account Balance and Account Transaction, feeding real-time account data in ISO 20022 format directly into ERP and TMS systems. Removing batch reporting delays tightens cash visibility and supports straight-through processing.

items.headline: Citi takes tokenised deposits live in seven markets with 24/7 clearing
items.summary: Citi's CEO reported on 13 October 2026 that Citi Token Services now runs tokenised deposits operationally across seven markets, letting institutional clients move blockchain-settled funds in real time with 24/7 clearing while keeping regulated banking status. Treasurers gain a route to out-of-hours liquidity moves.

items.headline: 47% of faster payment systems now support cross-border payments
items.summary: A Money20/20 survey finds 66% of RTGS systems run 24/7 or extended hours in 2026, up from 38% in 2023, while 47% of faster payment systems handle cross-border payments, mostly in APAC. Cut-off-driven liquidity buffers look increasingly dated.

items.headline: Auditors expected to test AI agents as internal controls, Forbes warns
items.summary: A Forbes Council article on 16 October 2026 says auditors will treat AI agents as governed configurations, requiring version control, segregation of duties so one identity cannot prepare and approve transactions, and fallback procedures. Each requirement will need evidence from Treasury and Finance.

items.headline: Deloitte and BDO set out AI governance for Finance Teams' reporting controls
items.summary: Deloitte and BDO have published guidance on AI governance in financial reporting, stressing transparency, data integrity, SOC reporting compliance and segregation of duties. The aim is auditor confidence in AI-enabled controls, which shapes how Finance documents data and validates models.

items.headline: FIRMA Advisory says FX hedging policies need explicit carry-cost thresholds
items.summary: FIRMA Advisory finds most corporate FX hedging policies have not been updated for divergent rate environments. Carry costs on multi-currency hedges are now material, so policies need explicit thresholds for each currency pair, giving treasurers a defined decision point.

items.headline: HSBC and MUFG research moves FX risk into the boardroom
items.summary: Research from HSBC and MUFG shows currency risk shifting from the back office to executive level, as trade tensions, tariff uncertainty and wider rate differentials raise volatility and hedging complexity. Boards will expect clearer FX exposure reporting from Treasury.

items.headline: ECB Pontes goes live for 24/7 DLT settlement in central bank money
items.summary: The ECB's Pontes platform went live on 21 September 2026, settling distributed ledger transactions in euro central bank money 24/7. DLT-based assets have sat inside the ECB collateral framework since March 2026, widening euro liquidity options for Treasury.

items.headline: Wider US-euro rate gap raises dollar funding costs for non-USD corporates
items.summary: Wider rate differentials between the US and EUR, plus structural dollar support from higher bond yields and trade and tariff uncertainty, are lifting funding and hedging costs for non-USD corporates that need dollar liquidity. Treasury budgets for USD borrowing face pressure.

items.headline: EU's largest sanctions package lists 1,569 targets in Russia's defence supply chain
items.summary: On 12 October 2026 the European Council adopted its largest-ever package, designating 1,569 targets: 826 Russian companies and 743 individuals serving as CEOs. The suppliers turn over €20+ billion annually and employ 250,000+ people, widening asset freezes and counterparty screening for payments and onboarding.

items.headline: ISSB proposes Practice Statement on nature-related disclosures under IFRS S1 and S2
items.summary: The ISSB published an Exposure Draft on 10 October 2026 for a Practice Statement on nature-related disclosures under IFRS S1 and S2. It would require disclosure of assets and activities vulnerable to those risks, integrated with climate-related disclosures and backed by SASB and TNFD metrics.

days.note_headline: Standard-setters now treat AI output as a claim Finance must prove in-period
days.note_opening: Standard-setters now treat AI output as a claim Finance must prove, not a fact. COSO 2026 classes GenAI output as an assertion and wants AI-assisted judgments documented during the reporting period, not after close. The

items.headline: Centalion's AI Treasury Agent on Komgo cuts amendment time by 80%
items.summary: Centalion Group's AI Treasury Agent, launched on Komgo on 8 October 2026, runs facility and trade Finance workflows in natural language under governance and approval controls. Amendment time fell 80% and issuance time 55%, freeing a projected 60 working days a year.

items.headline: FIS Agentic Insights Suite adds multi-horizon cash flow forecasting for Finance
items.summary: FIS released its Agentic Insights Suite on 12 October, pulling fragmented ERP, Treasury and CRM data into real-time scoring and forward-looking cash flow projections across multiple horizons. A plain-language interface serves Finance and Treasury teams, giving both one view of future cash.

items.headline: FIRMA Advisory ties operational cash thresholds to rolling 13-week forecasts
items.summary: FIRMA Advisory guidance sets operational cash thresholds at entity and group level, anchored to rolling 13-week forecasts so buffers move with the business cycle. It separates structural FX exposure from transactional noise and matches deployment to yield by currency via notional pooling, zero-balancing and target-balance structures.

items.headline: CPMI sets 2026-2027 timetable for ISO 20022 IP+ and HVPS+ guideline upgrades
items.summary: A BIS CPMI report schedules upgrades to the ISO 20022 IP+ instant and HVPS+ high-value usage guidelines for 2026-2027, aligned with ISO Message Release 2025 and full external code sets. pacs.028 Payment Status lands in 2026, camt.110/111 Investigation in 2027, both aimed at cross-border interoperability.

items.headline: COSO 2026 treats GenAI output as an assertion needing in-period evidence
items.summary: COSO 2026 says documentation for AI-assisted judgments must exist during the reporting period, not be created after close. ICFR controls need human-in-the-loop review, confidence thresholds, exception queues, escalation paths and monitored KPIs, because GenAI output counts as assertion, not fact.

items.headline: FSB finalises 12 AI sound practices with board accountability and vendor oversight
items.summary: The Financial Stability Board published 'Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence', setting 12 governance principles. Boards and senior management must set an AI approach aligned to business model and risk appetite, with strong governance over third-party AI vendors and reliance on them.

items.headline: HSBC and MUFG research moves FX risk from back office to boardroom
items.summary: HSBC research finds trade-policy uncertainty, geopolitical risk, supply-chain reconfiguration and higher interest rates reshaping corporate FX hedging. Treasurers are urged to reassess hedge ratios and tenors against carry costs, stress test for policy changes and automate exposure capture to cut manual process risk.

items.headline: Citi Token Services extends 24/7 tokenised deposit settlement to seven markets
items.summary: On 28 September, Citi expanded tokenised deposit settlement to seven markets, giving clients 24/7 transfers without cut-off times. Japan, supporting USD, and the UAE, supporting USD and Euro, join the US and UK, while Ireland, Hong Kong and Singapore complete the set.

items.headline: ECB holds at 2.50% as euro slides to 17-month low near 1.1130
items.summary: The ECB held at 2.50% on 29 October as surging energy costs raised upside inflation and downside growth risks. The euro fell to a 17-month low near 1.1130 USD as the French sovereign spread widened above 150 basis points and equity sell-offs fuelled safe-haven demand.

items.headline: OFAC sanctions A7 Network, blocking 435+ sub-agents across 83 countries
items.summary: On 24 October 2026, OFAC designated A7 Network a significant transnational criminal organisation used by Iran and others for sanctions evasion, blocking transactions with its 435+ sub-agents in 83 countries. FinCEN issued an alert and proposed treating A7-controlled transactions as a primary money laundering concern.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury - OFAC
FinCEN Alert on the A7 Network

items.headline: AICPA practice aid shows auditors how to test AI in internal controls
items.summary: On 13 October 2026, the AICPA released a practice aid for auditors assessing AI-related risks in financial reporting and controls, material misstatement and AI within internal control systems. It calls for professional scepticism towards AI outputs, given data quality and explainability concerns.

days.note_headline: Static Treasury policies are breaking, and Finance must rewrite them as live rules
days.note_opening: Treasury and Finance policies written for a zero-rate, batch-file world now produce wrong answers. FIRMA Advisory ties operational cash thresholds to rolling 13-week forecasts and builds explicit carry-cost thresholds in

items.headline: Agentic AI sweeps excess cash in near real time within authority limits
items.summary: Corporate treasuries are using agentic systems that watch balances across accounts, test projected needs against policy thresholds and sweep surplus cash into money-market funds or internal pools, reversing moves when payables need liquidity. Pre-set authority limits become the control that matters.

items.headline: BCG and Capgemini see Treasury AI agents reaching autonomous execution by 2026
items.summary: BCG and Capgemini describe agentic Treasury as a path from insight to signal, recommendation and execution, with autonomy by 2026 confined to low-risk, short-duration instruments. Larger decisions still escalate to people, so guardrails and audit trails decide how far agents go.

items.headline: TreasurUp and Apideck let banks reach 50+ ERP systems through one integration
items.summary: On 15 October 2026, TreasurUp and Apideck enabled banks to embed real-time ISO 20022 banking into 50+ ERP and accounting systems via a single, bank-branded integration on the bank's own rails. Treasurers gain live payment and account data inside the ledger.

items.headline: FIRMA Advisory links operational cash thresholds to rolling 13-week forecasts
items.summary: FIRMA Advisory anchors operational cash thresholds at entity level, consolidates them at group and ties them to rolling 13-week forecasts, so buffers move with the business. Static policies give way to dynamic liquidity rules that underpin working-capital deployment and sweep-and-pool structures.

items.headline: Real-time bank APIs replace overnight batch files with 15-minute syncs
items.summary: Bank connectivity is moving from batch-based reconciliation to event-driven webhooks and APIs that push transaction data and payment status into Treasury systems in 15-minute syncs. Reconciliation latency falls and near-real-time cash visibility becomes the baseline for liquidity decisions.

items.headline: Hackett finds record €1.26 trillion of excess European working capital
items.summary: Hackett Group's 2026 European survey, published in October 2026, puts excess working capital at a record €1.26 trillion, with receivables growing faster than revenue. Days sales outstanding worsened for a third consecutive year in 40 of 50 industries, so collections deserve Treasury and Finance attention.

items.headline: SWIFT defers structured postal address mandate for ISO 20022 messages
items.summary: On 27 August 2026 SWIFT postponed its November 2026 structured address requirement after market infrastructures asked for more time. Unstructured, hybrid and structured formats remain accepted until a revised deadline. Cross-border ISO 20022 coexistence ended in November 2025, so only address data gains time.

items.headline: EPC aligns address deferral as SCT Inst moves to 5-7-9 second execution
items.summary: The European Payments Council postponed the structured address requirement, aligning with the Nordic Payments Council and the revised market deadline. The latest SCT Inst rulebook cuts execution from 10-20-25 seconds to 5-7-9 seconds and removes the €100,000 default cap for B2B instant transfers.

items.headline: FSB finalises 12 sound practices for responsible AI adoption
items.summary: The Financial Stability Board published final guidance on 12 AI governance practices in October 2026, asking financial institutions to fold AI risks into existing risk frameworks, keep documentation and lifecycle records, and stage approvals by materiality. Board accountability and vendor oversight now reach Treasury AI.

items.headline: FIRMA Advisory adds carry-cost thresholds to FX hedging policy as rate gaps widen
items.summary: FIRMA Advisory says widening US-EUR rate gaps require explicit carry-cost thresholds by currency pair and horizon. Hedging a EUR 50 million receivable now carries a ~USD 1.1 million 12-month forward gain, versus ~€1 million in EUR receivable costs. Policies built for zero rates now mislead.

items.headline: EY finds 18% of corporates have used stablecoins, 15% tokenised deposits
items.summary: EY's blockchain payments study shows 18% of corporates have used stablecoins and 15% have deployed tokenised deposits, roughly doubling since 2025, with 21% using either for cross-border B2B payments. Supplier payments (53%) lead, aimed at cutting settlement delays (56%) and FX transaction costs (52%).

items.headline: BIS separates tokenised deposits from stablecoins on settlement finality
items.summary: The Bank for International Settlements defines tokenised deposits as account-based bank liabilities on programmable platforms that settle at par through central bank accounts, unlike stablecoins, bearer instruments on public blockchains without par enforcement. For Treasury, tokenised deposits offer greater interoperability and fungibility across banks.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%–4.00% as markets price 85.7% odds of December hike
items.summary: On 28 October the Fed held rates at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, two members preferring a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh signalled more increases. Derivatives price an 85.7% chance of a 25-basis-point December hike and three more quarter-point rises by September 2027, lifting refinancing costs.

items.headline: FinCEN and OFAC fine Bank of America record $1.2 billion over AML failures
items.summary: On 13 October 2026, FinCEN and OFAC penalised Bank of America $1.2 billion for weak anti-money laundering programmes, missing customer due diligence on correspondent accounts and late suspicious activity reports, including delays on $5+ billion in suspicious transactions. The scale shows how hard enforcement bites.

items.headline: FRC revises ISA (UK) 250 and 270 with risk-based non-compliance approach
items.summary: On 29 October 2026 the Financial Reporting Council published revised ISA (UK) 250 and ISA (UK) 270, setting a clearer, risk-based view of material misstatement from legal non-compliance, including Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 requirements. Audits from 15 December 2027 apply them.

days.note_headline: Money now moves at weekends, so Finance controls must run around the clock
days.note_opening: Weekends and holidays are becoming working days for corporate cash. JPMorgan's Wire 365 settles payments 24/7/365, including US holidays, while HKMA's Project Ensemble moved to 24/7 tokenised central bank money settlemen

items.headline: Ripple extends GSmart AI with policy-governed agents across Treasury workflows
items.summary: Ripple widened GSmart, its Treasury-native AI, in September 2026 to add policy-governed agents for forecasting, liquidity, risk, reconciliation and reporting. Every proposed action is checked against organisational policy before approval, and deterministic engines sit apart from AI interpretation, preserving control and auditability.

items.headline: HSBC launches HSBCnio with ISO 20022 APIs and Model Context Protocol access
items.summary: HSBC unveiled HSBCnio on 26 October 2026, an AI-enabled platform spanning web, mobile and API banking. Treasury teams can pull balances and transactions in ISO 20022 format, or connect their own AI tools through Model Context Protocol for read-only liquidity forecasting and variance analysis.

items.headline: Uber pilot earns 1.5 extra days of yield with 24/7 tokenised MMF settlement
items.summary: Uber tested 24/7 settlement of tokenised money market fund shares with HSBC and Franklin Templeton, backed by Tradeweb and Fireblocks (30 October 2026). Staying invested over weekends and redeeming out of hours with delivery-versus-payment finality delivered 1.5 additional days of yield over conventional liquidation.

items.headline: HSBC notional pool cuts Advanced MedTech external borrowing by up to $10 million
items.summary: Advanced MedTech pooled SGD, USD and EUR balances from 19 accounts across 8 entities into an HSBC multi-currency notional pool in Singapore. The structure lifted interest returns on idle cash, cut external borrowing by up to $10 million and funded working capital gaps intercompany.

items.headline: JPMorgan Wire 365 now settles cross-border payments 24/7/365
items.summary: JPMorgan has extended Wire 365 so payments can be initiated and settled 24/7/365, covering weekends and US holidays. The move answers corporate demand for round-the-clock settlement, helping treasurers manage working capital continuously and cut the risk of cash sitting idle.

items.headline: EY says AI audit readiness requires shared ownership across Finance, IT and risk
items.summary: EY's audit-readiness framework places AI governance inside existing risk assessment and ICFR scoping, not in a separate technology silo. Auditors will look for ownership across business units beyond data science, defined approval of model and prompt changes, and monitoring that stops inappropriate reliance on outputs.

items.headline: OAT-Bund spread hits 176bp, widest since late 2011, as euro slides
items.summary: On 23 October 2026 the French OAT-Bund 10-year spread reached 176 basis points (176bp), its widest since late 2011, while EUR/USD fell near 1.1130 on French budget worries and an energy shock, pushing up dollar funding costs for USD borrowers.

items.headline: HKMA's Project Ensemble moves to 24/7 tokenised central bank money settlement for 12 banks
items.summary: On 2 November 2026, the HKMA advanced Project Ensemble's pilot to settle interbank tokenised deposit transactions in tokenised central bank money 24/7, lifting participating banks from 6 to 12 and industry pioneers to 20. Treasurers gain real-time cash management and out-of-hours digital asset fund dealing.

items.headline: BoE hike to 4% dated 5 November; markets price 73% December Fed hike
items.summary: A Bank of England rise of 25 basis points to 4%, the first in over three years, is dated 5 November 2026 and awaits confirmation. The Fed held at 3.75%–4% on 28 October, with markets pricing a 73% probability of a December quarter-point hike.

items.headline: Euro climbs 0.48% to $1.1212 as oil eases and French spreads tighten
items.summary: EUR/USD rose 0.48% to $1.1212 on 2 November 2026 as oil fell on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy and the ECB gave clearer December guidance than the Fed. French spreads over Bunds tightened modestly, though fiscal risks keep longer-term euro weakness in play.

items.headline: Bank of America fined record $1.21 billion over AML and sanctions failures
items.summary: FinCEN and OFAC imposed a record $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America on 13 October 2026 for customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting failures, including over $5 billion in unreported transactions tied to Chinese money laundering networks and trade-based fraud.

items.headline: ISSB exposure draft proposes nature-related Practice Statement built on IFRS S1 and S2
items.summary: The ISSB issued an Exposure Draft on 22 October 2026 for IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Practice Statement 1, covering nature-related risks and opportunities. Built on IFRS S1 and S2, it captures any nature-related matter reasonably expected to affect cash flows, access to Finance or cost of capital.

sources.name: IFRS – ISSB consults on its proposals for nature-related disclosures
IFRS – Live from COP17: ISSB nature-related disclosures consultation

days.note_headline: Finance AI delivers real savings only where autonomy is bounded by design
days.note_opening: Agentic AI is producing measurable gains in Treasury and Finance, but only inside hard limits. Centalion cut trade Finance issuance processing by 55% and amendments by 80% on Komgo, with approvals still enforced at the o

items.headline: Centalion cuts trade Finance processing by up to 80% with Komgo agent
items.summary: Centalion deployed an AI Treasury Agent on Komgo, pairing a large language model with trade Finance workflows. Issuance processing for off-balance sheet instruments fell 55% and amendments 80%, freeing 60+ working days annually, while approvals stay enforced at the orchestration layer.

items.headline: Standard Bank CIB says agentic Treasury AI needs bounded autonomy
items.summary: Standard Bank CIB argues not every Treasury decision should be automated. Autonomy should sit on a spectrum from monitoring alerts to advisory, approval-stage and predefined execution within limits, with humans able to access assumptions and alternatives, because commercial judgment and accountability cannot be fully replicated.

items.headline: ServiceNow unifies 10+ Treasury data sources in Snowflake via Kyriba APIs
items.summary: ServiceNow's Project Artemis consolidated 10+ fragmented Treasury data sources, including TMS, ERP and banking portals, into a single Snowflake data lake. Kyriba APIs feed transactions, positions and cash balances directly into a governance-ready repository, giving Finance consistent reporting and analytics.

items.headline: Tipalti Treasury launches 13-week forecasts built from bank feeds and ERP invoices
items.summary: Tipalti released a Treasury solution that consolidates intraday and prior-day cash balances across entities and currencies with scheduled ERP payment data to produce customisable 13-week liquidity forecasts. Direct, secure global bank connectivity replaces manual aggregation across bank portals.

items.headline: Kyriba and J.P. Morgan embed Morgan Money liquidity recommendations in Treasury workflows
items.summary: Kyriba and J.P. Morgan have integrated Morgan Money into Treasury systems, surfacing liquidity recommendations shaped by each organisation's cash horizon, yield targets and funding needs. Suggestions respond to corporate context rather than hard-coded rules, so Treasury must decide how far to rely on them.

items.headline: Ant International runs 24/7 HKD liquidity on tokenised deposits via Ensemble TX
items.summary: Between September and October 2026, Ant International managed real-time cross-bank liquidity with BOCHK, CCB Asia and HSBC using tokenised deposits settled in central bank money on HKMA's Ensemble TX. HKD transfers took five minutes, giving 24/7 access and lower pre-funding.

items.headline: SWIFT requires structured postal addresses in cross-border messages from 14 November 2026
items.summary: From 14 November 2026, SWIFT requires structured postal addresses in ISO 20022 cross-border messages, and fully unstructured messages may be rejected or delayed. The EPC has aligned the SCT Inst rulebook with SWIFT's November 2026 MX Release, making address data a payment risk.

items.headline: FSB finalises 12 sound practices for responsible AI adoption
items.summary: The Financial Stability Board published its final report on 15 October 2026, setting out 12 non-binding practices spanning strategic direction, governance and human oversight, among others. Board accountability sits at the centre, and the toolkit is designed to adapt to institutions of all sizes.

items.headline: HSBC research moves FX risk from back office to boardroom
items.summary: HSBC research published on 6 October 2026 finds currency risk is now treated as a business-model issue rather than purely market risk. CFOs and treasurers are reassessing hedge ratios, stress testing for policy changes and automating exposure capture to strengthen resilience.

items.headline: Standard Chartered launches tokenised deposits for Hong Kong corporates on Ensemble TX
items.summary: Standard Chartered launched tokenised deposits for corporate clients in Hong Kong on 2 November 2026, pairing regulated bank deposits with programmability. Transfers between participating banks run in real time, with inter-bank settlement in central bank money 24/7 on HKMA's Ensemble TX.

items.headline: HashKey Group adopts Standard Chartered tokenised deposits for multi-market Treasury
items.summary: HashKey Group, an Asian digital asset company, has adopted Standard Chartered's tokenised deposit solution to run Treasury operations across multiple markets, using blockchain infrastructure for institutional-grade liquidity management and settlement. It gives the bank's offer a named corporate adopter.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% as JPMorgan forecasts December quarter-point hike
items.summary: The FOMC left rates at 3.75–4.00% on 1 October 2026, with two dissents favouring a hike. JPMorgan reads the statement as hawkish and expects a quarter-point increase in December, backed by strong US growth and 3.7% year-over-year inflation, a risk for floating-rate borrowers.

items.headline: FinCEN and OFAC fine Bank of America a record $1.21 billion
items.summary: On 13 October, FinCEN fined Bank of America $1.2 billion and OFAC added $11.6 million, a record $1.21 billion combined, for wilful AML/BSA violations and sanctions breaches. The bank missed SARs on $5 billion of suspicious transactions, with knock-on effects for corporate payment screening.

items.headline: AICPA practice aid maps AI risks to internal controls and misstatement
items.summary: The AICPA released a practice aid on 13 October 2026 to help auditors judge how AI in financial reporting and controls affects audit risk, covering data quality, model reliability, bias and hallucinations. That shows controllers where auditors will probe AI.

days.note_headline: Dearer money and real-time bank data leave trapped working capital nowhere to hide
days.note_opening: Idle cash has become an expensive habit for Treasury and Finance. The Bank of England raised rates to 4.00% on 5 November, its first hike in three years, and Hackett Group counts €1.26 trillion of excess working capital,

items.headline: HKMA launches Project SAGE to test agentic Finance in practice
items.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority set up Project SAGE on 2 November 2026 to help industry explore agentic Finance solutions and validate practical implementation challenges, with a focus on market development and regulatory dialogue. Treasurers get an early read on supervisory expectations.

items.headline: API-first Treasury systems replace overnight batches with intraday cash visibility
items.summary: Treasury management systems built on direct bank API integration refresh balances and transactions continuously through the day, normalise data across institutions and aggregate multiple entities. Replacing overnight batch processing gives Treasury a live cash position and an AI-ready data foundation.

items.headline: Embat connects to J.P. Morgan's Bank Account Services API for real-time data
items.summary: Embat's Treasury management platform now links to J.P. Morgan Payments through its Bank Account Services API, feeding balances, transactions and payment data into Treasury systems in real time. For J.P. Morgan clients on Embat, that means cash positions built from live bank data.

items.headline: Hackett Group finds €1.26 trillion trapped in European working capital
items.summary: Hackett Group's 4 November 2026 study of Europe's 1,000 largest firms puts excess working capital at €1.26 trillion, 14% of revenue. The cash conversion cycle improved 1.8 days in 2025, yet €113 billion remains releasable across payables, inventory and receivables. That is self-funded liquidity.

items.headline: ISO 20022 carries full remittance data across borders without truncation
items.summary: Under ISO 20022, payment and compliance data survive cross-border journeys intact, with remittance details landing in their original fields, untruncated and untranslated. Sender and receiver compliance teams therefore screen identical payment information, giving both ends a consistent view of every transfer.

items.headline: HKMA says agentic AI controls belong in the harness, not the prompt
items.summary: The Hong Kong regulator's 2 November 2026 Discussion Paper states that agentic AI controls must sit in the agent harness, meaning instructions, workflow design and permissions, rather than model-level guardrails or prompt engineering. Treasury and Finance agents need permissions designed in, not requested politely.

items.headline: FCA sets out good and poor practice for AI adoption in financial services
items.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority's framework calls for proportionate AI governance, senior management oversight, defined escalation triggers and multidisciplinary teams at the design stage. For Finance functions deploying AI, the point is plain: decide in advance when a human must step in.

items.headline: Treasurers shift FX hedging towards cash-flow-at-risk and fewer investor surprises
items.summary: Corporate treasurers increasingly report currency risk to boards through cash-flow-at-risk, quantifying the worst-case annual move in operating cash flow after hedges. The goal has moved from managing the earnings line to reducing investor surprises, putting predictability ahead of point-exposure protection.

items.headline: Tokenised deposits and stablecoins serve different Treasury jobs
items.summary: Tokenised deposits bring efficiency inside a single banking ecosystem and for internal cash pooling. Stablecoins keep the edge for cross-bank, multi-currency supplier payments and for bridging disconnected systems without common account relationships, so treasurers may need both rather than one.

items.headline: Bank of England lifts rates to 4.00%, its first hike in three years
items.summary: The Bank of England lifted rates 25 basis points to 4.00% on 5 November, its first rise in three years, amid rising energy costs. Gilt yields fell to six-week lows as markets expected policymakers to temper expectations of further hikes. Sterling floating-rate debt costs more.

items.headline: OFAC designates A7 Network, blocking 435+ sub-agents across 83 countries
items.summary: On 1 October 2026 OFAC designated A7 Network, linked to Russia and Iran sanctions evasion, a significant transnational criminal organisation, blocking dealings with 435+ sub-agents in 83 countries. FinCEN's proposed Section 9714 measure would bar covered financial institutions from fund transmittals involving any A7 Network Sub-Agent.

sources.name: Baker McKenzie Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

items.headline: FATF plenary moves to accelerate virtual asset standards implementation
items.summary: At its 28–30 October 2026 plenary, FATF agreed to significantly accelerate effective implementation of standards for virtual asset service providers in jurisdictions with materially important activity, citing rising ML/TF/PF risks and scam compound financing. Treasuries using stablecoins should expect tighter provider scrutiny.

items.headline: IASB seeks feedback on IFRS 9 hedge accounting by 26 January 2027
items.summary: The International Accounting Standards Board published a Request for Information on 28 September 2026 for its post-implementation review of IFRS 9 and IFRS 7 hedge accounting, with the deadline extended to 26 January 2027. It tests whether costs and benefits meet stakeholder expectations.

days.note_headline: Banks are wiring AI straight into Treasury data faster than Finance can govern it
days.note_opening: Banks are piping live account data straight into corporate AI, and Finance governance trails behind. HSBC's HSBCnio lets clients feed ISO 20022 data into their own AI via Model Context Protocol, and Embat now draws real-

items.headline: Ripple Treasury switches on fully autonomous mode for GSmart AI agents
items.summary: On 26 October 2026, Ripple Treasury let corporate customers configure GSmart AI agents to execute tasks such as overnight cash sweeps without routine approval. Policy controls, logging and escalation of edge cases to staff remain, so those limits now carry the risk.

items.headline: Embat links to J.P. Morgan's Bank Account Services API for intraday visibility
items.summary: Embat's Treasury platform now connects to JPMorgan's Bank Account Services API, feeding real-time balances, transactions and payment data into TMS and ERP systems. Overnight batch processing gives way to intraday cash visibility, sharpening positioning and liquidity decisions.

items.headline: NeuGroup: 23% of corporates leave over a quarter of operating cash idle
items.summary: NeuGroup's 2026 Corporate Cash Confidence Survey found nearly half of firms hold over 10% of operating cash uninvested and 23% leave more than a quarter idle. While 76% value 24/7 settlement, only 19% can move cash in real time. That gap costs yield.

items.headline: HSBC launches HSBCnio, opening ISO 20022 data to client AI systems
items.summary: On 29 September 2026, HSBC unveiled HSBCnio, an API-first transaction banking platform. Corporate clients can embed ISO 20022 data into their own AI systems through Model Context Protocol, with existing permissions and controls intact, bringing bank data closer to Treasury agents.

items.headline: BDO survey finds only 29% of organisations have formal AI governance policies
items.summary: BDO's 2026 Audit Innovation Survey found only 29% of organisations have formal AI governance policies with reduced manual reconciliation. Roughly 20% remain developing or ad hoc, and 17% say AI capabilities are outpacing their data infrastructure, a direct concern for controllers and auditors.

items.headline: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4%, first rise in over three years
items.summary: On 5 November 2026, the Bank of England's monetary policy committee voted 8–1 for a 25bp rise to 4%, citing rising inflation, now forecast to reach 5% by mid-2027, on Middle East energy prices. A wider USD-GBP gap lifts borrowing costs for non-sterling treasurers.

items.headline: Australian importers' FX hedging participation climbs to 87%, Commonwealth Bank finds
items.summary: Commonwealth Bank's FX Barometer, conducted August-September 2026, shows hedging participation rising to 87% for importers and 73% for exporters, as firms reassess expected AUD/USD weakness to 0.70 by end-March 2027. Corporates above A$4 billion turnover increasingly use options, forwards and cross-currency swaps.

items.headline: Deutsche Bank: tokenised deposits enable 24/7 settlement across branches
items.summary: Deutsche Bank's 2026 digital-money white paper shows tokenised deposit platforms on proprietary blockchain networks now support 24/7 settlement across branches. Programmable rule sets allow flexible cash pooling and rules-based automated sweeping, giving treasurers new options for structuring group liquidity.

items.headline: Euro holds near $1.12 as OAT-Bund spread narrows to 148bp
items.summary: On 5 November 2026, EUR/USD held around 1.1224, near $1.12, after earlier weakness, and the OAT-Bund spread compressed to 148bp from 176bp as French debt stabilised after the US midterm election. A widening rate gap keeps medium-term pressure on the euro.

items.headline: FATF launches targeted review to close virtual asset AML/CFT gaps
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, the FATF began a targeted review of jurisdictions with materially important VASP activity to close gaps in implementing virtual asset AML/CFT standards. Results follow in June and October 2027, a signal for treasurers holding or settling in digital assets.

items.headline: IASB opens IFRS 9 hedge accounting review, comments due 26 January 2027
items.summary: On 28 September 2026, the IASB published a Request for Information on IFRS 9 hedge accounting and IFRS 7 disclosures. The 120-day comment period closes on 26 January 2027, giving treasurers and controllers a chance to say whether benefits justify application costs.

days.note_headline: The bottleneck in Finance has moved from bank connectivity to forecasting discipline
days.note_opening: The bottleneck in Treasury and Finance has moved from getting bank data to using it well. Embat authenticates J.P. Morgan accounts in seconds through the Banking Authorization Service API, with no IT development required

items.headline: Embat links to J.P. Morgan BAS API for real-time bank data
items.summary: Embat clients can now authenticate J.P. Morgan bank accounts in seconds via the Banking Authorization Service API, with no IT development. Real-time balances, transactions and payment data feed Embat's ERP-integrated platform, cutting onboarding friction for Treasury visibility.

items.headline: J.P. Morgan accounts connect to Embat in seconds, without IT development
items.summary: Through J.P. Morgan Payments' Banking Authorization Service API, Embat's Treasury platform pulls real-time balances, transactions and payment data straight into its ERP-integrated system. Account authentication takes seconds and needs no IT development, shortening the path from bank to ledger.

items.headline: 62% of Finance executives struggle to manage or scale cash forecasting
items.summary: 62% of Finance executives report difficulty managing or scaling cash flow forecasting, which exposes gaps in liquidity visibility. Accurate forecasts depend on invoice timing, collection patterns and integration across disparate systems, the areas Treasury and Finance Teams must tighten.

items.headline: ECB moves TARGET Services address releases to 28 November 2026
items.summary: The ECB has pushed its November 2026 TARGET Services releases from 14 November to 28 November 2026 after SWIFT asked for more preparation time. The releases precede removal of unstructured postal addresses in cross-border messages, giving payment teams two extra weeks to fix address data.

items.headline: BDO finds only 29% of organisations have formal AI governance policies
items.summary: BDO's 2026 Audit Innovation Survey shows AI governance is still nascent, with 29% of organisations holding formal policies. Many rely on manual reconciliation and lack the data infrastructure for their AI ambitions, a gap that raises control and audit readiness concerns.

items.headline: Interest-rate derivatives hit record 14.78 million contracts daily in October
items.summary: In October 2026, interest-rate derivatives set a record monthly volume of 14.78 million contracts daily as the Treasury Volatility Index rose to 140. Corporates are buying more downside yield protection and tail risk cover amid funding market tightness and higher rate expectations.

items.headline: Uber earns 1.5 extra days of yield with HSBC tokenised deposits
items.summary: On 30 October, Uber completed a pilot using HSBC tokenised deposits on the Canton Network to buy and sell Franklin Templeton money market funds at weekends. Atomic delivery-versus-payment settlement outside traditional banking hours earned 1.5 extra days of yield on idle cash.

items.headline: EUR/USD hits 17-month low near 1.1159 after Fitch shifts France outlook
items.summary: On 2 November 2026, EUR/USD touched a 17-month low near 1.1159 after Fitch moved France's outlook to negative, with the OAT-Bund spread at 155-160 basis points. Euro weakness persists despite a softer dollar as eurozone growth diverges from the US.

items.headline: FinCEN bars MEXC Global over $16 billion in sanctions-linked flows
items.summary: On 6 November 2026, FinCEN ordered U.S. financial institutions to stop transacting with MEXC Global, a convertible virtual currency exchanger tied to at least $16 billion in Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion and cybercrime flows. Counterparty screening must reflect the order.

items.headline: AMLA finalises three standards on due diligence and group AML/CFT governance
items.summary: The EU's Anti-Money Laundering Authority published three final regulatory technical standards on business relationship classification, customer due diligence including PEP screening, and group-wide AML/CFT governance. The harmonised framework will shape corporate onboarding and counterparty screening across member states.

items.headline: ISSB opens 120-day consultation on nature-related disclosures Practice Statement
items.summary: In October 2026 the ISSB published an Exposure Draft of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Practice Statement 1 on nature-related disclosures, supplementing IFRS S1 and S2. The 120-day comment period closes on 19 February 2027, giving reporting teams time to respond.

days.note_headline: Auditors will judge Finance AI by existing control rules, not new ones
days.note_opening: AI in Finance has no rulebook of its own, so existing controls must carry the weight. PCAOB inspectors and peer reviewers test AI-driven controls under the ICFR framework, probing approval, validation, ownership and chan

items.headline: BCG says agentic AI in Treasury needs redesigned controls and escalation paths
items.summary: BCG finds Treasury operating models unready for autonomous decision-making at scale, with fragmented data and legacy governance built on human initiation. Thresholds and escalation paths must be embedded upfront, and accountability structures redesigned, before autonomy can scale safely.

items.headline: Huntington launches Intelligent Treasury platform with Kyriba for multi-bank visibility
items.summary: Huntington announced its Intelligent Treasury platform on 5 November 2026, built on Kyriba technology and cloud infrastructure. It delivers consolidated balances and transactions, daily-to-monthly forecasts, centralised payment workflows and ERP integration without major IT investment, giving Treasury multi-bank cash visibility.

items.headline: Real-time bank APIs displace overnight file transfers for intraday liquidity
items.summary: APIs now link bank platforms with ERP, TMS and payment systems continuously, replacing batch file transfers. They support real-time balances, payment initiation, tracking, validation, reconciliation and FX visibility, letting Treasury manage intraday liquidity without waiting on delayed settlement cycles.

items.headline: Kyriba named best Treasury management system in Euromoney 2026 awards
items.summary: Euromoney's 2026 awards named Kyriba best TMS for cross-bank data integration and ERP connectivity. The platform absorbs differing reporting standards across banks, integrates payables automation and handles multi-bank format and testing requirements in a single deployment, easing connectivity work for Treasury.

items.headline: Treasurers shift from cash optimisation to cash resilience amid volatility
items.summary: Treasurers are rethinking cash management around resilience: preserving liquidity through shocks, managing faster payment cycles, counterparty exposure control, fraud defence and cyber resilience, while still deploying surplus cash for yield. Return alone no longer defines a well-run cash programme.

items.headline: Fed aligns FEDWIRE, CHIPS and SWIFT for November 2027 ISO 20022 changes
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is coordinating FEDWIRE with CHIPS and SWIFT on ISO 20022 changes due in November 2027, keeping the networks interoperable as message formats evolve. Its phased timeline reflects migration complexity, giving Treasury a fixed date for bank and system readiness.

items.headline: PCAOB tests AI-driven controls under existing ICFR framework, not new standards
items.summary: PCAOB inspectors and peer reviewers are assessing AI adoption under existing audit documentation standards, with no separate AI category yet. They test technology approval, validation, ownership and change authority, so Finance must back AI controls with documented audit evidence and professional judgment.

items.headline: No AI-specific SOX standard exists, so CFOs must classify AI use
items.summary: Finance audit technology experts confirm there is no dedicated SOX or auditing standard for AI, though AI already drafts and reconciles within the financial close. CFOs need a classification framework that gauges how far each system sits from reportable decisions.

items.headline: Treasurers favour cash flow at risk over value at risk for FX
items.summary: Corporate FX hedging has shifted from protecting transactions to delivering earnings predictability. Cash flow at risk shows how far currency moves could push next-year operating cash flow below budget at a given confidence level, giving boards a clearer view of hedging cost and benefit.

items.headline: Ant International settles 24/7 HKD interbank transfers in tokenised central bank money
items.summary: On 2 November, Ant International completed live HKD interbank transactions using tokenised deposits settled in HKMA's Central Bank Money (CeBM) with BOCHK, CCB (Asia) and HSBC. Payments reached final settlement in under five minutes on a 24/7 basis, showing multi-bank Treasury automation working live.

items.headline: Fed December hike odds rise to 76–80% after strong October jobs
items.summary: On 6 November, traders lifted odds of a 25bp Federal Reserve hike at the December 8–9 meeting to 76–80%, from 67–75%, after 165,000 jobs were added, more than double forecasts, with unemployment at 4.1%. That repricing matters for floating-rate dollar debt.

items.headline: Bank of England lifts rates to 4.0% in first hike since August 2023
items.summary: On 5 November the Bank of England raised rates 25bp to 4.0%, its first increase since August 2023, by an 8–1 vote, citing higher energy prices and inflation momentum. CPI was 3.5% in September; the MPC forecasts 5% by Q2 2027, against a 2% target.

items.headline: FATF launches targeted review of virtual asset compliance gaps
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, FATF announced a targeted review of jurisdictions with materially important VASP activity, aimed at uneven implementation of virtual asset standards under R.15. Initial results come in June 2027, with follow-up in October 2027, relevant to any Treasury handling digital assets.

items.headline: ISSB opens 120-day consultation on nature-related disclosure Practice Statement
items.summary: On 22 October 2026 the ISSB published an exposure draft for a Practice Statement on nature-related disclosures, built on IFRS S1 and S2. The 120-day consultation closes on 23 January 2027; the guidance covers nature-related risks and opportunities affecting cash flows and cost of capital.

days.note_headline: Money now moves around the clock, but Finance controls still keep office hours
days.note_opening: Settlement has gone round-the-clock, and Treasury and Finance must now run controls on the same clock. Payments Canada launched its Real-Time Rail on 9 November 2026 with eight participants, including Bank of America, li

items.headline: Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital set out three-layer model for agentic payments
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital published agentic payments guidance with a three-layer architecture: intent and orchestration, control and authorisation, and settlement. Explicit limits, agent identity binding and Know Your Agent checks separate AI reasoning from execution, giving treasurers a template for approval design.

items.headline: Real-time bank APIs replace overnight batch files for intraday cash visibility
items.summary: Treasury teams are moving to API-first set-ups, swapping overnight file transfers for real-time bank connectivity. Event-driven feeds absorb high daily volumes asynchronously, while synchronous REST APIs handle instant payment approvals, giving intraday cash visibility and event-based reconciliation between TMS and ERP.

items.headline: Multiliquid Treasury offers 24/7 instant redemption on tokenised T-bill yields
items.summary: On 5 November, Multiliquid Treasury launched institutional cash management that lets corporate treasuries earn 3-month U.S. Treasury Bill yields on idle balances, with 24/7 instant redemption through tokenised assets. It targets the cash drag created by money market fund business-day cut-offs.

items.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail goes live with eight institutions and 24/7 settlement
items.summary: On 9 November 2026, Payments Canada launched the Real-Time Rail, offering instant exchange, clearing and settlement 24/7 on ISO 20022. Eight participants, including Bank of America, went live, with confirmation of payee and other fraud controls mandatory from day one.

items.headline: EY and COSO map AI failure modes onto existing SOX controls
items.summary: EY and COSO map AI risks, from hallucination and drift to prompt injection and agent over-autonomy, onto existing ICFR, with no new SOX standard. CFOs must classify uses, document validation, split configuration from approval and keep point-in-time logs of inputs, prompts and reviewer identity.

items.headline: MillTech survey finds corporate FX hedge ratios down to 46%
items.summary: On 18 September 2026, MillTech's survey showed US and UK companies cutting FX hedge ratios to 46%, the lowest since tracking began in Q1 2024. Average hedge length fell to 5.7 months, and nearly half of firms hedge only 26-50% of exposures.

items.headline: PNC Bank opens incoming USDC payments for corporate clients via Coinbase
items.summary: On 9 November 2026, PNC Bank launched incoming USDC payments for corporate and institutional clients in a Coinbase-powered pilot. Transfers on Ethereum convert automatically to U.S. dollars at a 1-to-1 rate into designated accounts, speeding cross-border receipts under full banking protections.

items.headline: Eurozone inflation hits 4.0%, making a December ECB hike highly probable
items.summary: On 4 November, eurozone inflation rose to 4.0% in October from 3.8% in September on food and energy costs. Markets price roughly 85% odds of a 25bp ECB hike on 17 December and two to three more hikes, potentially taking the deposit rate near 3.25%.

items.headline: Strong US jobs data lift December Fed hike odds to about 80%
items.summary: On 6 November, a stronger-than-expected US jobs report showed 165,000 new positions and 4.1% unemployment. Markets repriced December hike odds to about 80% from 67% on Thursday, with inflation still above the Fed's 2% target and policymakers wanting more data.

items.headline: FATF launches targeted review of virtual asset standards implementation
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, the FATF Plenary agreed a targeted review of jurisdictions with materially important virtual asset sectors, reporting initial results in June 2027 and more in October 2027. It addresses uneven implementation of VASP standards that criminal networks exploit.

items.headline: ISSB opens 120-day consultation on nature-related disclosure Practice Statement
items.summary: In October 2026, the ISSB opened a 120-day public consultation on a proposed Practice Statement for nature-related disclosures. It would complement IFRS S1 and S2 with guidance on governance, strategy, risk management, and nature-related metrics and targets, widening reporting scope for Finance.

days.note_headline: Agent autonomy in Finance is a standing control cost, not a launch project
days.note_opening: Autonomy in Treasury and Finance is becoming a design choice that carries a running cost. JPMorgan frames agentic AI as 'fly-by-wire', with humans setting boundaries and agents adjusting within them, while Trovata on Ama

items.headline: JPMorgan likens agentic Treasury AI to fly-by-wire flight controls
items.summary: JPMorgan casts Treasury autonomy as policy-bounded execution: people set boundaries and permissions, and agents make continuous adjustments inside them. The catch for treasurers is that thresholds, auditability and escalation paths must be designed upfront, before any agent is allowed to act.

items.headline: Trovata builds autonomous Treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
items.summary: Trovata, working with AWS, has built an AI-native Treasury solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore that reconciles hundreds of accounts automatically, cutting manual processing from hours to seconds. It also enables autonomous cash-management workflows, shifting the control question from doing reconciliations to supervising them.

items.headline: Citizens Bank launches Treasury Intelligence for multibank cash and forecast views
items.summary: Citizens Bank unveiled Treasury Intelligence on November 9, 2026, consolidating cash positions and forecasts across all of a client's banking relationships. A basic version is available to AccessOPTIMA reporting clients, giving treasurers one view of cash across every bank relationship.

items.headline: EuroFinance 2026 turns Treasury focus to cash trapped in operating cycles
items.summary: Treasurers at EuroFinance 2026 moved past cash optimisation towards releasing cash locked in operating cycles. Receivables management, payment terms, inventory control and process automation took centre stage, putting cash conversion firmly on a shared agenda between Treasury and the wider Finance function.

items.headline: ISO 20022 carries remittance data across rails but leaves interoperability gaps
items.summary: The shared ISO 20022 standard lets remittance data travel across instant-payment systems without truncation. Global interoperability is still held back by differing field requirements and address formats between regional real-time rails, and the standard does not solve currency conversion or liquidity prefunding.

items.headline: FEI and Controllers Council test AI as both system and preparer
items.summary: The Financial Executives Institute and Controllers Council propose assessing AI within the existing COSO framework. As a system, AI is judged on access, configuration, monitoring and model updates; as a preparer, its output gets the same management review as human accounting work.

items.headline: KPMG tells CFOs AI safety is a lifecycle cost, not a launch cost
items.summary: A KPMG executive warns that AI spending does not stop at testing and validation. Continuous red-teaming, runtime observability, security controls, incident response and human oversight run for the life of the system, so safety belongs in recurring budgets, not one-off project spend.

items.headline: Forvis Mazars and EY test whether ICFR controls still fit AI
items.summary: Forvis Mazars and EY map AI's audit implications onto existing SOX and COSO frameworks, asking whether ICFR controls stay appropriate as AI takes on financial tasks. New expectations may follow for authorisation, data quality, monitoring, incident response and third-party oversight.

items.headline: Diverging BoE and ECB paths call for separate sterling and euro hedging
items.summary: EuroFinance analysis suggests the Bank of England may hike in early 2027, while the ECB adjusts in December and then eases. Sterling and euro exposures need separate management. Floating-rate sterling debt merits urgent review, with phased hedging and caps protecting borrowers while keeping optionality.

items.headline: OCBC and Ant International launch 24/7 tokenised-deposit settlement in SGD and USD
items.summary: OCBC is the first bank to partner with Ant International on tokenised deposits, delivering near-real-time SGD and USD settlement on a 24/7 basis across Singapore and Malaysia via the blockchain-based WhaleRTP platform. Less reconciliation and freed trapped liquidity are the Treasury gains.

items.headline: Deloitte sees 3.5% UK inflation keeping Bank of England hike expectations high
items.summary: Deloitte's October-November rates and FX newsletter puts UK headline inflation at a persistent 3.5%, driven by energy, which keeps rate-hike expectations elevated. BoE and ECB policy paths diverge significantly, with distinct consequences for sterling and euro borrowers through early 2027.

items.headline: FinCEN cuts MEXC Global off from U.S. financial system over $16 billion flows
items.summary: On 6 November 2026, FinCEN barred U.S. financial institutions from transmittals of funds to or from MEXC Global. The cryptocurrency exchanger processed at least $16 billion in illicit transactions tied to Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion and cybercrime. Payment screens must block it.

items.headline: ISSB opens 120-day consultation on nature-related disclosure practice statement
items.summary: The ISSB published an Exposure Draft of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Practice Statement 1 on 9 October 2026, opening a 120-day consultation with comments due 19 February 2027. It guides disclosure of material nature-related information affecting cash flows and cost of capital.

days.note_headline: Record operating cash is masking slower collections, and rising rates will expose it
days.note_opening: Headline cash strength across Treasury and Finance is hiding a deterioration in collections. Hackett's survey of the 1,000 largest North American companies shows operating cash flow at 17% of revenue, a 13-year high, whi

items.headline: Centalion and Komgo cut trade-finance issuance time 55% with an AI agent
items.summary: Centalion Group and Komgo deployed an AI Treasury agent that answers natural-language queries on trade-finance facility capacity, enforces controls through an orchestration layer and keeps human approval at every step. Issuance time fell 55%, amendments 80%, freeing 60+ working days yearly.

items.headline: Prolific Banking's FI-Streams portal cuts bank API rollout to under four months
items.summary: On 9 November 2026 Prolific Banking launched the FI-Streams Developer Portal and APIs, letting banks offer branded self-service APIs to corporates in under four months rather than 12–18 months. Payments, reporting and webhooks are covered, shortening Treasury's wait for connectivity.

items.headline: Hackett finds receivables up 11%, twice revenue growth, as DSO slips again
items.summary: Hackett's 2026 survey of the 1,000 largest North American companies put operating cash flow at 17% of revenue, a 13-year high. Receivables rose 11%, twice revenue growth, DSO worsened 2.1 days for a third year, and the cash-conversion cycle improved only 0.2 days.

items.headline: Only 38% of CFOs see better customer payment behaviour, down from 73%
items.summary: 52% of CFOs now prioritise clearer cash-flow views, yet only 38% report improved customer payment behaviour, down from 73% a year earlier. Supply-chain programme settlement volumes rose 35% year-on-year, suggesting vendor-payment deferral is reaching its limits as a working-capital lever.

items.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail goes live with 8 participants and 24/7 settlement
items.summary: Payments Canada launched Real-Time Rail on 9 November 2026, offering 24/7 interbank clearing and settlement on ISO 20022 with immediate funds availability. 8 institutions, including Bank of America and Wealthsimple, joined at launch; a Canada-EU RTR link is under discussion but not yet operational.

items.headline: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 maps AI risk to 16 components across six pillars
items.summary: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 sets out an AI supervisory framework of 16 components across six pillars: purpose, risk, control, oversight, resilience and assurance. It creates no new enforceable standards but applies existing risk-management concepts, signalling examiners will evaluate material AI use.

items.headline: Bank of England lifts Bank Rate to 4.00%, first rise since August 2023
items.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% in November 2026, its first increase since August 2023, with markets pricing up to three more hikes. Sterling treasurers face December hike risk, while euro treasurers may see a December adjustment before eventual ECB easing.

items.headline: EY finds corporate stablecoin use doubled to 18% in live production
items.summary: EY's July–August 2026 survey found 18% of corporates running stablecoins live in production, double the 9% of 2025. Only 5% of financial institutions have no plans to offer stablecoin services, with cross-border supplier payments and B2B acceptance leading use cases.

items.headline: U.S. Q3 GDP grows 3.4%, reinforcing the Fed's higher-for-longer stance
items.summary: U.S. GDP expanded at a 3.4% seasonally adjusted annualised rate in Q3, driven by resilient domestic spending and strong capital investment. Firm employment data support the Fed's higher-for-longer stance into the final months of 2026, leaving little near-term rate relief for dollar borrowers.

items.headline: FATF finds only 34% of jurisdictions largely compliant on virtual assets
items.summary: On 5 November 2026 the Financial Action Task Force published its seventh targeted update, finding only 34% of jurisdictions largely compliant with virtual asset AML/CFT standards. Gaps in Travel Rule operationalisation and enforcement affect corporate payments routed through digital asset channels.

items.headline: IASB keeps IFRS 16 intact but tightens lease cash outflow disclosures
items.summary: Concluding its post-implementation review on 28-29 October 2026, the IASB found IFRS 16 working as intended. It will strengthen disclosure of total cash outflows for lease payments and how they are classified across operating, investing and financing activities, sharpening cash-flow reporting.

days.note_headline: The SEC wants proof behind Finance AI claims, and spreadsheets still run cash
days.note_opening: AI claims across Treasury and Finance now need evidence that matches daily practice. The SEC set up a Financial Reporting and Accounting Unit in August 2026, and Enforcement Director David Woodcock said on 30 October 202

items.headline: Atlar deploys Claude-powered agents for OnePay's scheduled Treasury workflows
items.summary: On 12 November 2026, Atlar put Claude-powered autonomous agents to work in OnePay's Treasury operations, running scheduled cash position analysis and bank fee audits with approval controls. Agents connect to all OnePay banks and its ERP, showing how sign-off gates keep autonomy accountable.

items.headline: Huntington and Kyriba launch Intelligent Treasury for multi-bank cash visibility
items.summary: Huntington announced Intelligent Treasury, built with Kyriba, as of 5 November 2026. It offers consolidated balances and transactions, daily-to-monthly cash forecasting, centralised payment workflows and ERP integration across multiple banking relationships, giving treasurers one view of cash across their banks.

items.headline: Finmo board finds 80–90% of Asia cash positioning still runs on Excel
items.summary: Finmo's advisory board found 80–90% of Asia cash-position work runs on Excel fed by portals, emails, ERPs and Treasury systems. Multi-entity consolidation is hardest, as accounting platforms are single-entity by design and lag 1–2 weeks in transaction coding.

items.headline: Citigroup urges treasurers to classify jurisdictions to free trapped cash
items.summary: Citigroup's liquidity guidance asks treasurers to sort jurisdictions as liberal, semi-restrictive or restrictive. The aim is better cash visibility, mobilising trapped cash and building market-based concentration frameworks, giving groups a structured basis for deciding where liquidity can realistically be pooled.

items.headline: BIS says G20 end-2027 cross-border instant-payment goal is unachievable
items.summary: Instant-payment rails on ISO 20022 still diverge on message versions, field requirements and address formats, forcing translation between them. The BIS December 2025 assessment confirms the G20 end-2027 cross-border goal is unachievable despite policy completion, so cross-border friction will outlast the deadline.

items.headline: SEC to test whether AI use matches public disclosures in 2027 exams
items.summary: A new SEC Financial Reporting Unit will assess whether AI use aligns with public disclosures, focusing on fair representation, operational consistency and whether algorithm recommendations match investor profiles. Heightened 2027 examination priorities put AI governance squarely on the CFO office's agenda.

items.headline: KPMG tells CFOs AI governance is a lifecycle cost, not a launch cost
items.summary: KPMG argues strong AI governance speeds enterprise adoption, but generic AI-leader claims need verifiable support that stays consistent across earnings releases, calls and filings. The CFO office must build those controls upfront rather than retrofit them, budgeting governance across the whole lifecycle.

items.headline: CME interest-rate derivatives hit record 14.8 million contracts a day in October
items.summary: CME Group said on 3 November 2026 that October 2026 interest-rate derivative average daily volume reached 14.8 million contracts, up 28% year-over-year, with U.S. Treasury futures up 48%. Corporates and asset managers are hedging diverging central bank rate paths and persistent energy-driven inflation.

items.headline: Zanders and Standard Chartered say tokenisation beats 2–3 day correspondent settlement
items.summary: Joint analysis from Zanders and Standard Chartered finds that tokenising cash, deposits, securities and collateral as programmable blockchain tokens enables near-real-time settlement, against 2–3 day correspondent-banking cycles. That cuts reconciliation effort and frees trapped liquidity.

items.headline: Markets price 87% chance of December Fed hike after hot October CPI
items.summary: Headline CPI of 0.4% and core CPI of 0.3%, both above consensus, on 10 November pushed markets to price an 87% probability of a 25 basis-point hike on December 9, up from 72% a week earlier. Governor Christopher Waller backed a quarter-point rise.

items.headline: Euro slides to 18-month low at 1.1095 as rate gap widens
items.summary: EUR/USD hit 1.1095, an 18-month low, as 10-year US Treasury yields stood above 5% on 11 November 2026 after the hot October CPI print, while ECB hike odds stayed lower. The wider US-eurozone rate differential raises the stakes for euro-dollar hedging.

items.headline: FinCEN cuts MEXC Global from US system over $16 billion in flows
items.summary: On 6 November 2026, FinCEN ordered covered financial institutions to stop moving funds to or from Seychelles-based crypto exchange MEXC Global, citing $16 billion in sanctions-linked flows tied to Russian illicit Finance and cybercrime. The order, effective 10 December 2026, tests onboarding and counterparty screening.

items.headline: SEC Enforcement to scrutinise whether corporate AI disclosures match reality
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, SEC Enforcement Director David Woodcock said the Division will test whether AI disclosures represent capabilities and material risks. A Financial Reporting and Accounting Unit from August 2026 pursues accounting fraud, auditing misconduct; 2027 priorities cover AI claims and audit committee oversight.

days.note_headline: Costlier hedging and slower customer payments make working-capital resilience the Finance priority
days.note_opening: Working capital is becoming harder and dearer to defend across Treasury and Finance. Only 38% of CFOs polled by PYMNTS report better customer payment behaviour, against 73% a year earlier. Sikich found 48% of 183 Finance

items.headline: Trovata deploys autonomous Treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
items.summary: Trovata has put autonomous agents to work in Treasury operations on Amazon's Bedrock and AgentCore platforms, covering cash forecasting, variance analysis and anomaly detection without extra development work. The question for treasurers is who reviews agent decisions before they shape cash positions.

items.headline: Kyriba Open APIs connect live Treasury data to 1,000+ banks and ERPs
items.summary: Kyriba's Open APIs feed live Treasury data and financial workflows straight into enterprise applications, with a Developer Portal offering 1,000+ bank integrations, ERP and partner links, a full API catalogue and an App Marketplace. More connections mean more access rights for treasurers to govern.

items.headline: Only 38% of CFOs see better customer payment behaviour, down from 73%
items.summary: A PYMNTS survey finds just 38% of CFOs report improved customer payment behaviour, against 73% a year earlier, as procurement teams use extended terms as a competitive tool. Treasurers are moving from optimising cash towards building working-capital resilience against volatility.

items.headline: Rate volatility and working capital each worry 48% of Finance leaders
items.summary: Sikich surveyed 183 Finance leaders in August–September 2026: 48% named interest-rate volatility and 48% named working-capital optimisation as top Treasury concerns, while 42% worried about access to capital. The results frame 2027 funding plans around rate risk and liquidity.

items.headline: FedNow adds ISO 20022 cross-border capability and payee name verification
items.summary: The FedNow Service has launched an ISO 20022 message format capability and a payee name verification API to support cross-border pilot operations. It lays groundwork for instant payments across jurisdictions, and name checks give treasurers an extra control against misdirected funds.

items.headline: IAASB publishes first quality management guide for AI-enabled audit tools
items.summary: The IAASB has released its first quality management guidance for AI-enabled tools in audit and assurance engagements, answering global calls for consistency as firms apply AI to high-stakes financial judgements. For controllers, it sets the bar audit firms must meet when AI touches their numbers.

items.headline: RBI's 20% cash reserve on FX derivatives makes Indian dollar hedging dearer
items.summary: India's RBI introduced a foreign-exchange risk reserve (FERR) on 10 October 2026, requiring banks to hold a 20% cash reserve against eligible FX derivative contracts. One-year forward premia reached 4.85% by mid-October before easing to 3.91%, making dollar hedging dearer for treasurers.

items.headline: Banque de France outlines private clearing for tokenised deposits via Pontes
items.summary: Banque de France First Deputy Governor Denis Beau set out a hypothetical private-sector clearing mechanism for tokenised bank deposits that would settle through the Pontes wholesale service. The aim is to keep central-bank money central in Europe as dollar stablecoins grow.

items.headline: All 71 economists expect ECB to lift deposit rate to 2.75% in December
items.summary: All 71 economists Reuters polled on November 10–12 expected the ECB to raise its deposit rate to 2.75% in December; over one-third see another hike in Q1 2027. With eurozone inflation at 4%, treasurers must plan for diverging euro and dollar rate paths.

items.headline: OFAC extends Cuba sanctions to electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology sectors
items.summary: On 4 November 2026, OFAC expanded Executive Order 14404 authority to Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology sectors, allowing designation of foreign persons active there. Coverage already spanned energy, defence, metals, mining, financial services and security, so counterparty screening scope must widen.

items.headline: SEC Enforcement to test AI disclosure accuracy in 2027 examinations
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, SEC Enforcement Director Woodcock signalled closer scrutiny of whether firms' AI use matches Form ADV disclosures and marketing materials. Examinations in 2027 will test the accuracy of claims, operations against disclosures and whether algorithms advise in line with investor profiles.
